samples.summary: The change flips `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` to enforce-by-default and rewrites three docs to say so, but leaves the canonical share-link and template-gallery docs asserting the opposite default, so the design corpus now gives two answers to "is a viewer's write refused on a stock deployment?"
samples.evidence: docs/design/sharing.md:208-219 still reads "This is **off by default**. `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` is unset in a stock deployment, which puts the controller in shadow mode… in the default one the client-side `readOnly` flag is the write boundary", and 184-186 / 230-235 repeat it ("with the flag at its default the client-side checks are what stands there"). docs/design/template-gallery.md:668 likewise: "with `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` unset the auth webhook only *shadows*". docs/design/README.md:155 still summarises the webhook as "shadow→enforce rollout". The diff updates only yorkie-auth-webhook.md, notes/notes.md and slides/slides-mobile.md — and notes.md:307-324 explicitly records the shadow-default claim as the thing that was wrong, which is exactly the sentence left standing in sharing.md and template-gallery.md.

samples.summary: sharing.md is the canonical per-type read-only doc for share links, and the new cross-cutting rule this change introduces ("nothing on a read-only mount may reach `doc.update()`" — presence, seeds, migrations, recalcs, comment mutators) is recorded only in notes.md and slides-mobile.md, not in sharing.md's sheet/docs sections or comments-mentions.md.
samples.evidence: sharing.md:151-192 enumerates exactly what a read-only sheet and docs mount blocks; the diff adds several new blocks there (YorkieStore presence seed / updateSelection / ensureAxisOrder, `assertWritable` on the five comment mutators, `Spreadsheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas`, `CommentPopover readOnly`, `YorkieDocStore(doc, readOnly)` presence suppression, `PdfCollabProvider initialRoot`, board selection presence) with no corresponding doc edit. comments-mentions.md:251 discusses anonymous/share-link viewers and says nothing about comment writes being refused for a signed-in viewer, which is the case this change fixes.

samples.summary: `readOnlyNoteStore` is a near-verbatim copy of `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts` (~150 lines of security-relevant Proxy traps) rather than a shared generic helper, and the two have already diverged in this very change.
samples.evidence: Both files carry the same reader-allowlist rationale, the same `get`/`set`/`defineProperty`/`deleteProperty`/`getPrototypeOf`/`setPrototypeOf`/`preventExtensions`/`isExtensible`/`has`/`getOwnPropertyDescriptor`/`ownKeys` traps, the same non-configurable-property carve-out, the same memoization map and the same `batch(fn)` special case, largely word-for-word. The new copy adds a `READ_ONLY_VIEWS` WeakSet for idempotency and a `HISTORY_METHODS` null-returning case; the docs copy has neither, so a trap fix or idempotency fix landing in one will not reach the other. Only the readers set and the two special cases are genuinely per-package; the trap machinery is store-interface-agnostic and could live in a shared module. Mitigating context: docs/design/shared-core-extraction.md:84 marks "Store abstraction" a Non-Goal for `@wafflebase/core`, and `@wafflebase/notes` does not depend on core today — so this is reuse that was available, not required.

samples.summary: A comment added by this change states the opposite of what the same change does — it says the Yorkie auth webhook "ships in shadow (allow-all) mode by default".
samples.evidence: The new block comment above `EditorState.readOnly.of(readOnly)` reads: "since the Yorkie auth webhook ships in shadow (allow-all) mode by default and so may not refuse the write either", while `packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts` added in the same diff makes enforcement the default and notes/notes.md records the shadow-default claim as an error being corrected. The sibling wrapper's comment (packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:39-42, out of diff) carries the same now-false premise and was not updated, even though its notes twin's comment was rewritten specifically to fix it.

samples.summary: A third hand-rolled reading of `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` is added instead of calling the shared assertion its own comment points at.
samples.evidence: The added comment says "The same explicit affirmation the server demands at submit/approve — see assertYorkieAuthEnforced", and then re-implements the literal check `config.get('YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE') !== 'true'` with its own message. `assertYorkieAuthEnforced(enforce)` in packages/backend/src/template/template-review.ts is a pure function taking `string | undefined` and is directly callable here. The change otherwise centralises the other reading into `isYorkieAuthEnforced`, so this is the one copy left to drift when the affirmation semantics change again.

samples.summary: The change bundles unrelated CI-flake fixes (and a repo-wide auth posture flip) with the notes share-link toolbar issue it is nominally for, which mixes independently-revertible concerns in one diff.
samples.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260907-notes-share-toolbar-lessons.md:1 frames the branch as "notes share-link toolbar (issue #1044)". Alongside that work the diff carries: a DuckDB extension-download warm-up in packages/backend/test/lakehouse-parity.e2e-spec.ts (WARMUP_TIMEOUT_MS), editor-disposal teardown in packages/docs/test/view/large-paste-indicator.test.ts and update-style-to-match.test.ts, and the enforce-by-default + `yorkie-service` token workstream across backend, scripts and five frontend surfaces. None of the three test-infra items relates to notes share links or to webhook enforcement; the enforcement flip is a deployment-posture change whose rollback story is now entangled with a toolbar fix.
